title: Ten Jurisdictions Complete the Inaugural Administration of the NextGen Uniform Bar Examination
author: National Conference of Bar Examiners

kp.k: NextGen bar examination completes its first operational administration
kp.d: In its 31 July 2026 press release, NCBE reports that 2,640 examinees completed the inaugural NextGen UBE across 10 jurisdictions and 16 testing locations, following eight years of development. The document concerns professional admission assessment and testing technology; it does not make claims about AI.
qs: The inaugural administration of the NextGen Uniform Bar Examination (NextGen UBE) was held this week, marking the first operational administration of the new examination.
In total 2,640 examinees successfully completed the first administration of the NextGen UBE across 10 jurisdictions and 16 testing locations.

The administration marked the culmination of eight years of research, development, and collaboration between the National Conference of Bar Examiners (NCBE) and the legal education community, courts, bar admission agencies, practicing attorneys, psychometricians, accessibility experts, and technology partners.

kp.k: Venue infrastructure prevented 647 Washington applicants from testing
kp.d: NCBE attributes Washington's disruption to a venue-specific infrastructure issue at the Yakima Convention Center, where approximately 700 applicants were scheduled to test. Most could not start, and the Washington State Bar Association canceled testing for affected applicants after unsuccessful efforts to resolve the issue. Preliminary figures distinguish 647 applicants unable to test from 28 nonappearances and 3 incomplete attempts among approximately 3,318 registrations overall.
qs: In Washington, where approximately 700 applicants were scheduled to test, most were unable to start the examination because of a venue-specific infrastructure issue at the Yakima Convention Center.

Despite extensive efforts by jurisdiction staff, testing-site personnel, and technical support teams to diagnose and resolve the issue, the Washington State Bar Association ultimately determined that it could not proceed with the administration and canceled testing for the affected applicants.

Approximately 3,318 applicants registered for the examination. Of those, 28 did not appear for the exam, 3 did not complete their attempts, and 647 were unable to test in Washington because of the venue issue.

kp.k: Contingency measures supported testing amid localized technical problems
kp.d: NCBE reports that first-day network bandwidth problems at certain Maryland and Missouri locations were resolved, allowing scheduled completion. Across 131 testing rooms, contingency measures included redundant networks, staggered starts, mobile hotspots and backup devices. Approximately 4% of examinees received backup devices for routine technical problems distinct from localized disruptions. NCBE asserts that there were no systemic platform issues and commits to reviewing operational and technical data before future administrations.
qs: Certain testing locations in Maryland and Missouri experienced site-specific network bandwidth issues on the first day of the administration. Those issues were resolved, allowing examinees to complete testing as scheduled.
The examination was administered across 10 jurisdictions, 16 testing locations, and 131 testing rooms.
Contingency measures, including backup devices, redundant networks, staggered starts, and mobile hotspots, helped jurisdictions continue testing when localized issues arose.

Backup devices were distributed to approximately 4% of examinees to address routine technical issues unrelated to the localized disruptions experienced at certain sites, allowing testing to continue with minimal disruption.
There were no systemic platform issues, and the NextGen platform performed as designed.

NCBE will continue reviewing operational and technical data in partnership with participating jurisdictions, testing sites, and technology providers and will incorporate those findings into preparations for future administrations.

kp.k: Preliminary applicant feedback favored content and platform experience
kp.d: NCBE reports positive preliminary survey responses about examination content and the platform's modern design and non-linear format, including many responses from applicants who experienced delays. The release supplies no survey sample size or quantified satisfaction results; these are preliminary reported perceptions rather than findings about assessment validity.
qs: Preliminary survey responses, many of which reflected the experiences of applicants who encountered testing delays, indicate that examinees nevertheless responded positively to both the content and the testing platform experience, citing the platform's modern design and the flexibility of the non-linear testing format.

kp.k: Examination targets seven foundational legal practice skill areas
kp.d: NCBE describes the examination as measuring seven foundational areas spanning research, writing, analysis, investigation and evaluation, counseling, dispute resolution and client management. Separately, Connecticut Bar Examining Committee chair Hon. Anne C. Dranginis (Ret.), quoted by NCBE, expresses confidence that the exam better reflects the knowledge and skills new attorneys need across practice areas. That endorsement is the committee chair's assessment, not a reported comparative validation result.
qs: Building on the proven foundation of the Uniform Bar Examination, the NextGen UBE measures proficiency in seven foundational skill areas: legal research, legal writing, issue spotting and analysis, investigation and evaluation, client counseling and advising, negotiation and dispute resolution, and client relationship and management.
The CBEC has confidence that this exam better reflects the fundamental knowledge base and skill sets that new attorneys should have across practice areas they enter the practice of law.

kp.d: The release announces that 13 named jurisdictions will join the NextGen UBE beginning in July 2027 and states that a total of 52 jurisdictions will begin administering it between the release and July 2028. These are prospective rollout commitments, distinct from the inaugural administration's operational results.
qs: Beginning with the July 2027 administration, Arizona, Iowa, Kentucky, Minnesota, Nebraska, New Mexico, North Dakota, Oklahoma, South Dakota, Tennessee, Vermont, West Virginia, and Wyoming will join the jurisdictions already administering the NextGen UBE.
A total of 52 jurisdictions will begin administering the NextGen UBE between now and July 2028.
